weeks.context: This week you are going to build Hydra — a small water-tracking app. 8 glass icons on the screen. Tap one to mark it filled. By Sunday it will run on YOUR phone as a real installed app, not just a preview. If you have never built an app before, that is fine. Every step is given.

items.title: Sketch Hydra
items.body:
Hydra is a water tracker. 8 glass icons on screen. Tap a glass — it fills. Tap again — it empties. There's a counter saying 'X / 8 glasses today'. When you hit 8, a small '✨ You hit 8' message appears.

On a piece of paper or in a notes app, sketch what this looks like. 1 minute. Just so you have the picture in mind.

items.title: Hello, phone
items.body:
STEP 1 — Install Node.js. Open the Node.js card, download LTS, install (click Next on every screen).

STEP 2 — Install Expo Go on your phone (App Store or Play Store).

STEP 3 — Open a terminal (Anaconda Prompt on Win, Terminal on Mac).
      cd Desktop
      npx create-expo-app@latest hydra --template blank
  This downloads about 100MB. Takes 2-3 minutes. When done you have a 'hydra' folder.

STEP 4 — Start the app.
      cd hydra
      npx expo start
  YOU SHOULD SEE: a big QR code in your terminal.

STEP 5 — Scan the QR code.
  ANDROID: open Expo Go on your phone, tap 'Scan QR code', point at the terminal.
  IPHONE: open the Camera app, point at the QR code, tap the notification.
  YOU SHOULD SEE on your phone: 'Open up App.js to start working on your app!'
  Your computer and your phone must be on the same WiFi for this to work.

items.title: Make it pretty
items.body:
STEP 1 — Add SafeAreaView so content doesn't go under the iPhone notch.
  At the top of App.js, change the react-native import to:
      import { StyleSheet, Text, TouchableOpacity, View, SafeAreaView } from 'react-native';

STEP 2 — In the JSX, replace the OUTER <View style={styles.container}> with <SafeAreaView style={styles.container}>. Match the closing tag too.

STEP 3 — Add a reset button. After the celebrate Text, before </SafeAreaView>, add:

      <TouchableOpacity style={styles.resetBtn} onPress={() => { setGlasses([false,false,false,false,false,false,false,false]); AsyncStorage.removeItem('hydra-glasses'); }}>
        <Text style={styles.resetText}>Reset</Text>
      </TouchableOpacity>

STEP 4 — Add styles for the reset button. Add to StyleSheet.create:

      resetBtn: { marginTop: 40, paddingHorizontal: 30, paddingVertical: 12, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: '#0284c7', borderRadius: 8 },
      resetText: { color: '#0284c7', fontSize: 14, fontWeight: '600' },

STEP 5 — Test the reset button. Fill some glasses, tap Reset, all empty.

days.title: Build the APK and ship
days.summary: Today you make a real installable app file and push to GitHub.

items.title: Expo account — sign up (free)
items.why: Click 'Open' to sign up. Needed to build an APK.

items.title: Build APK and push
items.body:
STEP 1 — Sign up for Expo (free).
  Open the Expo signup card. Make an account.

STEP 2 — Log in from the terminal.
      npx expo login
  Enter your Expo email + password.

STEP 3 — Build an APK (Android installable file).
      npx eas build --platform android --profile preview
  It asks a few questions — accept the defaults.
  It takes 10-15 minutes (build runs in the cloud — free tier).
  When done, you get a URL ending in .apk

STEP 4 — Install the APK on your phone.
  Open the build URL on your phone. Download the .apk.
  Android: tap to install. You may need to allow 'unknown sources' in Settings.
  Open the app — it runs standalone, no Expo Go needed.

STEP 5 — Push to GitHub.
  Open the 'create new repository' card. Name: hydra. Public.
  In your terminal (in hydra folder):
      git init
      git add .
      git commit -m "Hydra v0.1 — water tracker"
      git branch -M main
      git remote add origin https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/hydra.git
      git push -u origin main

STEP 6 — README.
  Add a README.md to the repo with:
    - The APK download URL
    - A screenshot of the app on your phone (take one!)
    - 'Install instructions'
  Push again.

PASS CRITERIA — Hydra v0.1 ships when:
  ☐ App runs on your phone, 8 glasses tap to fill
  ☐ Reset button works
  ☐ State survives app close (AsyncStorage)
  ☐ '✨ You hit 8 today.' appears at 8
  ☐ Real APK file exists from EAS build
  ☐ GitHub repo has the code + README + screenshot

Common patterns — swipe to delete, pull to refresh, parallax header, bottom sheet
Performance — keep work on the UI thread; never run gesture math on JS
Lottie — pre-made animations from After Effects
